hook_text: No rivers, no rain for months, and temperatures over forty degrees. How do people live there?
clip_script: The Eye of Kuruman: clear water bubbling out of the ground in the dry Northern Cape. Water is everything in a desert. Tuareg herders in the Sahara move their camels and goats from well to well. San hunter-gatherers in the Kalahari stored water in ostrich eggshells. Oasis farmers grow dates under palm trees. Today, desert cities use air conditioning, deep wells and even sea water made fresh. Every desert lifestyle begins with finding water.
visual_style: Whiteboard desert scenes in four panels: a camel caravan, a San hunter with an ostrich eggshell, an oasis with date palms, and a modern city with solar panels.
mood: Respectful and curious, celebrating human cleverness.
pacing: One lifestyle at a time, each answering water, food, shelter and clothing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and compare two desert lifestyles in a table: water, food, shelter and clothing.
